policies.title: Brazilian nationals: outside the foreign VIVIS regime
policies.summary: The QGRV governs entry of foreigners; a Brazilian national is therefore outside its foreign visitor-visa classification.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish the document requirements for a particular Brazilian national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual national presents a different country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: QGRV-listed ordinary passports: VIVIS visa exemption
policies.summary: For these ordinary national passports, the QGRV VIVIS column records a visa dispensation for a short visitor stay. China is handled by the later country-specific MRE update.
conditions: The QGRV legend limits this policy to the VIVIS column for holders of ordinary passports. PADIP (diplomatic) and PASOF (official or service) columns are separate and are not normalized here.

The precise dispensation period is the numbered VIVIS entry and applicable footnote in the QGRV, rather than a single uniform duration; the table uses 30-, 60-, 90-, 180-, and other specified periods.
A QGRV # marker permits entry with a civil identity card for the marked nationality. This passport classification neither requires nor generalizes that separate identity-card facility.
This policy does not cover a laissez-passer, refugee or alien travel document, diplomatic, official, service, public-affairs, temporary, or other special passport/document.

Visa dispensation is not a residence authorization and does not authorize paid work. VIVIS is limited to visitor purposes; a different purpose, a longer stay, or residence requires the applicable immigration route.

Admission and the authorized stay remain subject to Brazilian border control and all current entry requirements. Any extension is a separate Polícia Federal process and depends on the applicable QGRV reciprocity rule.

policies.title: China ordinary passports: VIVIS visa exemption
policies.summary: MRE's current Zurich consular guidance says Chinese ordinary passport holders have been exempt from VIVIS since 11 May 2026 for the specified short-visit purposes.
conditions: The MRE guidance limits the exemption to multiple-entry tourism, business, transit, artistic, or sports visits, for at most 30 days in one year.
Longer stays and other purposes require the appropriate physical visa under the MRE guidance.

This applies to an ordinary Chinese passport; it does not establish treatment of a PRC Travel Document, Hong Kong SAR passport, Macao SAR passport, Taiwan passport, diplomatic passport, official passport, or another special document.
The consular page's country-specific online filing note does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa category for this normalized visitor classification.

policies.title: Australia, Canada, and United States ordinary passports: electronic VIVIS
policies.summary: Australia, Canada, and United States nationals require a Brazilian visitor visa from 10 April 2025 but may obtain the nationally described electronic visitor visa.
conditions: The MRE source describes this as a visitor visa (VIVIS), not visa-free entry; it is valid only for the visitor purposes and periods the visa grants.
The electronic route is expressly described by MRE for these three nationalities. Generic online consular processing for other nationalities is not normalized as eVisa.
This policy is limited to ordinary national passports and does not establish a rule for diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, alien, or other special travel documents.
A visitor visa does not establish residence or permission for paid employment; entry and admission remain subject to Brazilian immigration control.

application.label: Brazil electronic visitor visa application
steps: Use the MRE-linked electronic visitor-visa application site.
Complete the visitor-visa application and provide the requested supporting documents.
Receive the electronic visa before travel and present it with the ordinary passport used for the application.

policies.title: QGRV-listed ordinary passports: VIVIS required
policies.summary: For these ordinary national passports, the QGRV VIVIS column records that a Brazilian visitor visa is required before the short visit.
conditions: This is limited to the QGRV VIVIS column for an ordinary passport. It does not infer a rule from PADIP, PASOF, residence status, special passport, laissez-passer, refugee document, or alien travel document.
The required visa is a visitor visa; purpose, length, and entry conditions are assessed under the visa and ordinary migration rules, and the visa does not itself authorize residence or paid work.
For Haitian nationals, the later MRE notice says QGRV was updated to require prior consultation with MRE Brasília for VIVIS. That additional case-management condition remains applicable.
For Taiwan, the QGRV's distinct treatment is document-specific; this ISO-code policy does not establish admission on a Taiwan diplomatic, official, or special passport.

policies.title: Mexican nationals: outside foreign visitor visa scope
policies.summary: INM's nationality lists regulate foreign nationals' visitor admission, not Mexican citizens.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish document requirements for an individual Mexican national, dual national, carrier, or border route.
It does not determine treatment when a dual Mexican national presents another country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: INM-listed ordinary passports: visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: The listed nationalities may seek admission as visitors without permission to undertake remunerated activities without obtaining a Mexican visa in advance.
conditions: This policy is for a visitor without permission to undertake remunerated activities, including tourism; it does not grant residence, work authorization, or a right to admission.

INM may verify passport or internationally valid identity-and-travel document, travel purpose, accommodation or itinerary, means of subsistence, departure transport, and other relevant information at migration review.
The visitor period is not a guaranteed 180 days: INM authorizes the period at entry, and the visa-required guidance says the non-resident visitor route may not exceed 180 days.
For a land entry, INM requires the applicable completed FMM; international-airport FMM handling is generated through migration control.

This normalization is limited to ordinary national passports. It does not establish rules for residence cards, diplomatic or official documents, refugees, stateless persons, alien travel documents, or other special documents.

policies.title: Russia, Türkiye, and Ukraine: SAE electronic authorization for air visitors
policies.summary: Russian, Turkish, and Ukrainian ordinary passport holders may obtain the SAE pre-travel electronic authorization to fly to Mexico as non-remunerated visitors, instead of first obtaining a Mexican visa.
conditions: SAE is an air-only pre-travel authorization for a visitor without permission for remunerated activities; travel by land or sea requires a Mexican visa under INM's current SAE guidance.

The traveller needs a valid passport, an approved authorization, a participating airline, and a printed authorization for airline and migration checks. Approval does not guarantee admission or the period authorized at entry.

The INM central SAE page says the authorization is valid for 30 days and one entry. A current Mexican consular post in Milan instead states 180 days and one entry; the validity conflict is recorded here and the central INM statement is used operationally pending clarification.

A valid visa of Canada, Japan, the United States, the United Kingdom, or a Schengen country, or permanent residence in the listed countries (including Chile, Colombia, and Peru), is a separate alternative to both Mexican visa and SAE for a visa-required national.
This policy does not establish residence, remunerated activity, ordinary visa-free entry, or a rule for diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, or other special travel documents.

application.label: INM Sistema de Autorización Electrónica
steps: Complete the INM electronic-authorization request with the valid ordinary passport.
Print the approved authorization before presenting at the participating airline's check-in counter.
Present the authorization and passport for Mexican migration inspection on arrival by air.

policies.title: Brazil: electronic visa for air visitors
policies.summary: From 5 February 2026, Brazilian ordinary passport holders may use Mexico's electronic visitor-visa route for a non-remunerated stay of less than 180 days when entering exclusively by air.
conditions: Mexico's Rio consular guidance calls this route a visa electrónica. It is normalized as eVisa rather than ETA because approval produces a visa and the official application charges a visa fee.
The route is exclusively by air, for fewer than 180 days and without remunerated activities. It is valid for one entry; the Rio source states 180 days' authorization validity.
A Brazilian transit traveller using this route must obtain a new electronic visa each time the traveller disembarks at a Mexican airport.
A residence visa, multiple-entry visa, ten-year visa, land or sea entry, remunerated activity, or other purpose requires the applicable separate Mexican process.
Electronic authorization does not guarantee admission; Mexican migration authorities decide admission and the authorized visitor period at the point of entry.

application.label: Mexico electronic visa application for Brazilian travellers
steps: Complete the electronic visa form using the details from the valid Brazilian passport.
Upload the required face photograph and passport data-page image, then pay the application fee.
Receive the electronic visa before travel and present it with the same passport for the air journey and migration inspection.

policies.title: INM-listed ordinary passports: visitor visa required
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require a Mexican visa for travel as a non-remunerated visitor unless the traveller holds a specifically listed alternative document or qualifies for another documented exception.
conditions: INM says the listed nationalities must obtain the visa corresponding to their condition of stay at a Mexican consulate; for tourism, business, or other non-remunerated activity this is visitor without permission for remunerated activities.

A valid and current visa of Canada, Japan, the United States, the United Kingdom, or a Schengen country is an alternative to a Mexican visa. Permanent residence in Canada, the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom, a Schengen country, Chile, Colombia, or Peru is another alternative.

An ABTC approved by Mexico is an alternative only for air entry and business travel. Aircraft crew certification and a seafarer's book for qualifying crew are separate document-specific alternatives; an air-arriving seafarer also needs proof of enrolment, vessel data, and the Mexican port.

These alternatives do not create nationality-wide visa-free status and do not establish residence, paid work, or admission. The ordinary visitor stay cannot exceed 180 days absent residence or a migration process.
This policy concerns ordinary national passports only. It does not establish a rule for diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, alien, or other special travel documents.

policies.title: Swiss SEM short-stay visa exemption for listed national passports
policies.summary: SEM List 1 marks each listed nationality as not requiring a visa for a stay of up to 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary/national passport scope only; the SEM table's document and V1 annotations remain controlling.
