policies.summary: The named second-list nationalities may use Oman’s 14-day visa exemption only when the stated third-country-visa/residence or GCC-resident-profession condition is met.
conditions: The traveller must meet the same passport-validity, return-ticket, confirmed-hotel, health-insurance, and sufficient-funds conditions as the general 14-day exemption.

The national must either be a resident of, or hold a valid entry visa for, the United States, Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Japan, or a Schengen country; alternatively, the national may be a GCC resident in a qualifying resident-visa profession.
The stay is limited to 14 days and cannot be extended or transferred to a residence visa.
This is not unconditional visa-free access. It does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa, visa-on-arrival, employment, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, or special-document route.

policies.title: GCC citizens: Oman visa-free entry
policies.summary: Citizens of the named Gulf Cooperation Council states do not require visas to enter Oman.
conditions: This policy follows the Foreign Ministry’s GCC-citizen rule and does not state a maximum visitor stay, an employment entitlement, or treatment of GCC residents who are not GCC citizens.
GCC residents of another nationality are instead subject to the separate conditional exemption’s qualifying-profession rule.
Diplomatic, official, service, special, emergency, travel-document, residence, work, purpose, and individual-admission requirements are not established by this ordinary-passport classification.

policies.title: Jamaican nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: PICA's country table governs foreigners and Commonwealth nationals entering Jamaica, not Jamaican nationals.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish a particular traveller's document, carrier, dual-nationality, departure, residence, or admissibility treatment.
It must not be read as resolving entry when a dual Jamaican national presents another country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: PICA-listed ordinary passports: visa exemption for a short visit
policies.summary: PICA's live country table expressly marks these ordinary-nationality cohorts as not requiring a visa for entry to Jamaica; the stated duration and permitted short-visit purpose vary by row.
conditions: This is a nationality-specific ordinary short-visit exemption, not a finding that every PICA-listed document is visa-free. The exact table rows set differing stays and purposes: many state 30 or 90 days, the United States row states six months, and China and Macao are tourism-only examples.

PICA attaches health-document conditions to Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Slovenia, and attaches yellow-fever proof conditions to Bolivia, Paraguay and Peru. Those document conditions remain applicable and do not change the normalized visa-free status.

The specific Dominican Republic and Ireland rows also cover ordinary, diplomatic and official passports for stated tourism, business, cultural, transit, official, or diplomatic purposes. This policy only models the ordinary-passport short-visitor part of those rows.

A visa exemption neither authorizes work, residence, study, crew duties, nor overrides any purpose-specific requirement. It does not establish treatment of diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, alien, certificate-of-identity, laissez-passer, military, seaman, or other non-ordinary documents.

MFAFT states that an immigration officer at the port of entry has final authority. Travellers must also use a valid, approved travel document; the embassy guidance adds passport validity for the visit and yellow-fever evidence when travelling from or through a WHO risk country.

policies.title: PICA-listed ordinary passports: visa at port of entry
policies.summary: PICA expressly says that these nationalities require a visa but may obtain it at the port of entry; this is normalized as visa on arrival, not visa-free or eVisa.
conditions: This route is limited to the PICA rows that literally state a visa may be obtained at the port of entry. It is not a general online-visa or prior-approval route.

Taiwan's row requires an Affidavit of Identity in addition to the port-of-entry visa. PICA's page separately says that holders of other accepted non-passport travel documents generally require a visa.

MFAFT says port-of-entry visa applicants must satisfy immigration authorities of their bona fides; its published checklist includes a valid passport, onward or return ticket and sufficient funds/accommodation. Admission remains for the immigration officer to decide.
The policy does not establish diplomatic, official, refugee, alien-document, residence, work, study, crew, transit, or any unlisted-special-document treatment.

policies.title: PICA-listed ordinary passports: visa required before travel
policies.summary: PICA's current country table requires a visa for these ordinary-passport cohorts and does not give them the port-of-entry visa route; the MFAFT-hosted Immigration Unit listing expressly supplies Timor-Leste as PTA.
conditions: For Albania, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Honduras, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania and Serbia, PICA's country-specific text gives a narrow visa waiver for a tourist stay of 30 days or less only when the traveller holds the named valid United States, Canadian, United Kingdom or Schengen visa, with listed vaccination evidence where required. That is a third-country-document condition, not passport-wide visa-free access or a Jamaican visa on arrival.

Kosovo's PICA row requires both a visa and an Affidavit of Identity. Haiti and Cuba retain the table's diplomatic/official passport exceptions, which do not alter their ordinary-passport prior-visa classification.

The current PICA row for the United Arab Emirates says visa required. A 2019 MFAFT announcement described an interim UAE port-of-entry arrangement pending an online system; the later live PICA table is used as the current operational rule, and this historical discrepancy is retained in the related snapshot conflict.

MFAFT instructs a person whose passport nationality requires a visa to apply at the Jamaican consular post where they live or the nearest one. Visa possession does not guarantee admission; purpose, work, residence, transit, document and immigration-admissibility rules remain separate.

MFAFT separately says a person visiting as part of a cruise does not need a visa, while an unrecognised-country national needs an Affidavit of Identity. This travel-mode or document exception is not a passport-wide ordinary visitor status and does not change this cohort.

No generic eVisa or ETA is inferred from the availability of consular processing. This policy does not establish treatment of special, diplomatic, official, refugee, alien, emergency, travel-document, crew, or resident classes.

application.label: Jamaica MFAFT visa guidance
steps: Confirm the nationality and document rule in PICA's country table.
Apply to the Jamaican consular post in the country of residence or nearest Jamaican consular post.
Do not travel on the assumption that a visa guarantees admission; present all applicable entry documents to immigration.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports that do not require a visa
policies.summary: DGI expressly places these nationalities in its no-visa entry category.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality classification only. DGI's country list says these nationals do not require a visa to enter Zambia.

For air arrival, non-citizens/non-residents need a valid return air ticket; for land or water arrival, they need funds for their stay and departure. Admission remains subject to immigration examination.
This does not establish access for diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless or other special travel documents, residents, workers, students, crew, or case-specific travel.
Transit, including direct airside transit, and purpose-specific requirements are separate rules.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports eligible for visa on arrival
policies.summary: DGI expressly allows these nationalities to get a visa at any Zambian port of entry.
conditions: DGI states these nationalities may receive a visa on arrival at any port of entry or from selected Zambian missions.
The same page says they may apply online, but that optional online route does not replace the expressly available arrival-visa route or make this a nationality-wide eVisa classification.

For arrival issuance, DGI requires host information and a physical Zambia address, a passport valid at least six months from entry with at least three full blank pages, and either a return air ticket or sufficient funds for land/water arrival.
Purpose, residence, employment, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document and individual admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports requiring prior-clearance eVisa
policies.summary: DGI requires these nationalities to apply online and receive an approval letter before travelling to Zambia.
conditions: DGI says this category requires advance clearance, online application through eServices, and an approval letter before travel; it cannot use a visa-on-arrival route.
The electronic approval is an eVisa for the model's pre-travel-entry category; it does not guarantee admission, which remains subject to immigration examination.
Bring the approval letter and receipt to entry. DGI states eVisa approval-letter holders may enter through any port of entry.
DGI notes that applicants under 16 cannot make an eVisa application themselves and must be included in an adult's application when travelling with an adult.
Does not decide special documents, diplomatic/official treatment, residence, employment, study, crew, transit or case-specific purpose rules.

application.label: Zambia Department of Immigration eServices visa application
steps: Create or use an eServices account and select the visa application.
Complete Form 16, upload the required documents, review the application and pay online.
Receive and print the approval letter before travel; present the letter and receipt to the Immigration Officer.

policies.title: Ecuadorian nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: The Human Mobility Regulation's tourist-entry rules govern foreign persons, not Ecuadorian nationals presenting an Ecuadorian passport.
conditions: This classification does not establish entry treatment for dual nationals presenting another passport, residence, migration-registration, departure, document-validity, or individual-admissibility requirements.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: transitory visitor eVisa required before travel
policies.summary: Effective 1 September 2025, Ecuador's foreign ministry expressly requires the named nationalities to obtain the electronically issued Visa de Visitante Temporal de Transeúnte before entering Ecuador.
conditions: The announcement calls this authorization a Visa de Visitante Temporal de Transeúnte under the 2025 reform to Article 66 of the Organic Law on Human Mobility. It must be requested while the applicant is outside Ecuador through the ministry's official digital service.

The Foreign Ministry describes the eVISAS service as electronic visas processed 100% online. Its current guide says the approved electronic visa is sent by email for the traveller to download and present, so this is normalized as eVisa rather than a non-electronic advance visa, ETA, or visa on arrival.

The foreign ministry's visitor regulation separately provides that a tourist may not perform work or economic activity. Passport validity, visa validity, purpose, route, residence, transit, diplomatic or official document, security, prior immigration history, and border-admission requirements remain separate and are not established by this nationality rule.

application.label: Ecuador Foreign Ministry digital visa service
steps: Apply for the transitory temporary visitor visa from outside Ecuador through the ministry's digital service.
Provide the documents and pay the amounts required for the individual application.
Download the eVisa delivered by email and present it with all required documents to migration control; issuance does not itself establish admission.

policies.title: Named South American ordinary passports: visitor entry up to 180 days
policies.summary: The current exhaustive required-visa list does not include these named South American nationalities, and the Human Mobility Regulation allows South American tourists up to 180 days in a year.
conditions: The 180-day figure is the maximum that migration control may grant to a South American tourist in one year; it is not a guaranteed stay or an authorization for employment or economic activity.

The classification rests on the Foreign Ministry's explicit current list of all nationalities for which Ecuador requires a visa, read with the visitor-stay rule. It does not establish national-identity-card use, residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.

Entry remains subject to presenting an identity-verifying travel document, migration-control verification of the invoked status, security and admissibility requirements, and any current health or carrier requirements.

policies.title: Other expressly unlisted ordinary foreign passports: visitor exemption up to 90 days
policies.summary: Ecuador's foreign ministry expressly identifies the complete current nationality list for which a visa is required; the other named foreign ordinary-passport codes are therefore visitor-exempt for the regulation's normal maximum of 90 days in one year.
conditions: This complement is inferred only from the ministry's explicit current statement that the listed countries are those whose nationals are required to hold a visa. The current source does not state a nationality-wide eVisa, ETA, arrival-visa, or electronic travel-authorization route for this complement.

A foreign tourist may remain for a maximum of 90 days from the first entry in a year and may apply once for an extension of up to 90 further days under the regulation. This normal 90-day rule does not replace the distinct South American maximum.

The traveller must present a travel document verifying identity and satisfy the migration-control officer that the claimed immigration status applies. No work or economic activity is authorized by tourist entry.

This is limited to ordinary foreign passports. It does not establish diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, laissez-passer, residence, employment, transit, special-purpose, or individual security/admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Argentine nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: DNM's tourist visa matrix applies to foreign passport nationalities, not Argentine nationals.
conditions: This classification does not establish the documents, carrier requirements, dual-national treatment, exit conditions, or admission decision for a particular Argentine national.
It does not resolve entry when a dual national presents a different country's ordinary passport.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: DNM's exhaustive ordinary-tourist passport matrix has no visa requirement in the ordinary-passport column for these nationalities.
conditions: This is limited to the DNM matrix's ordinary-passport tourist column. Blank ordinary-tourist cells are treated as the table's express visa-exempt entry rule; no complement is inferred.

A tourist enters for rest or recreation, is normally authorized for up to three months, may request one comparable extension, and may not perform remunerated work. Transit, frontier transit, crew, academic, medical, special, work, study, and residence are separate Migration Law categories.

Mercosur and associated-national rows remain ordinary visa-exempt entries, but DNM separately permits Brazil, Bolivia, Uruguay, Paraguay, Chile, Peru, Venezuela, Ecuador and Colombia to use specified valid national identity or travel documents. This passport policy does not extend that document option to other nationalities.

The ordinary-passport table separately shows diplomatic/service outcomes for some nationalities. This policy does not establish diplomatic, official, service, refugee, alien, emergency, laissez-passer, certificate-of-travel, residence, or other special-document treatment. Admission and any separate health, carrier, or border control requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: China, Dominican Republic and India: conditional ordinary tourist visa exemption
policies.summary: Current 2025 Argentine resolutions waive both a consular visa and AVE for these ordinary passports only when the traveller presents the specified valid United States visa and stays within the stated tourist/business scope.
conditions: China and Dominican Republic require an ordinary passport plus a valid, current United States visa of a similar migratory category. Dominican Republic is tourist-only, up to 90 days; China is tourist or the specified business category, up to 30 days.

India requires an ordinary passport plus a valid, current United States visa of a similar migratory category, verified as required; it is tourist-only and up to 90 days. Its rule took effect 28 August 2025.

These are conditional exemptions, not general visa-free status for the passport codes. A person outside the stated conditions must obtain a consular visa; no change of migratory category is allowed and a single comparable extension remains subject to DNM assessment.

DNM's AVE portal also mentions a United States green card for China, while Resolution 316/2025's operative text specifies a valid United States visa. The resolution is treated as controlling for this legal condition; the portal wording is preserved as an operational discrepancy for review.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: AVE electronic travel authorization
policies.summary: The listed ordinary passport nationalities are eligible to seek Argentina's AVE electronic travel authorization instead of a consular tourist visa only when they meet DNM's additional United States document and history requirements.
conditions: AVE is an electronic travel authorization, not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival. It applies to valid ordinary passports travelling as tourists, only for nationalities in DNM's current AVE list.

An applicant must hold a valid United States B2, J, B1, O, P, E or H-1B visa covering the AVE processing, AVE validity and intended Argentine stay. A person from a United States visa-exempt jurisdiction may instead show a verified U.S. entry in the preceding two years, a valid ESTA, or one of the stated visas.

DNM says an AVE tourist authorization is valid for three months, permits a three-month tourist stay from first entry with multiple entries/exits, and may be extended once after DNM assessment. DNM has up to 20 working days to decide and may extend that period.

Taiwan's ordinary-tourist matrix row states 'visa / travel certificate'; AVE eligibility does not erase document-recognition or certificate requirements. The same caution applies to every diplomatic, official, service, special, refugee, alien, residence, work, study, crew, transit, or other non-ordinary-document case.
Approval is not guaranteed. Complete the fee step and online application through DNM; do not enter before the authorization is issued.

application.label: Argentina DNM AVE Global
application.processingTime: DNM states up to 20 working days for tourist AVE decisions, extendable when necessary.
steps: Confirm that the passport nationality is on DNM's current AVE list and that the additional United States eligibility evidence is valid.
Use DNM's AVE portal to pay the fee and submit the online application.
Wait for DNM's decision before travelling; an AVE is not an arrival-issued visa.

policies.title: DNM-listed ordinary passports: consular tourist visa required
policies.summary: DNM's exhaustive ordinary-tourist matrix expressly marks these nationalities 'REQUIERE VISA' or a visa/travel-certificate requirement. Any separate AVE or 2025 conditional United States-visa exception is retained as a narrow overlapping route, not silently converted into general visa-free access.
conditions: This policy consists only of DNM's explicit ordinary-tourist rows marked 'REQUIERE VISA' (and Kosovo/Taiwan's 'visa / travel certificate' rows). It is not a nationality complement inferred outside the official matrix.

China, India and the Dominican Republic have the separate conditional United States-visa tourist exemptions in the other policy; all three still display as visa-required in the matrix for travellers without that exception. The AVE-eligible countries likewise remain visa-required if the AVE conditions or authorization are absent.

For the consular tourist visa route, Argentina's official service guidance requires a passport valid for at least six months, a completed application, financial proof, return reservation, accommodation/itinerary or invitation, fee and consular interview. Apply through the Argentine consular representation with jurisdiction.

The tourist category is for rest/recreation, normally up to three months and renewable once; it does not permit remunerated work. Transit, crew, work, study, residence, diplomatic/official/service, refugee, special travel certificate and other Migration Law categories are separate and cannot be inferred from this ordinary-passport policy.

application.label: Argentina tourist visa guidance
steps: Confirm the ordinary-passport rule and whether a separate AVE or statutory conditional exemption applies.
Contact the competent Argentine consular representation to arrange the required tourist-visa interview.
Submit the official travel, financial, passport, itinerary/accommodation and other consular documents before travel.

policies.title: Nepal: Indian ordinary passports with no visa required
policies.summary: TIA Immigration expressly says Indian citizens do not need a visa to enter Nepal.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality result only. TIA Immigration says Indian citizens may enter using a valid passport without a visa.
The source also describes voter-card and minor-document alternatives for Indian citizens without a passport; those document-specific routes are outside this ordinary-passport policy.
Does not decide residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, or case-specific entry rules.

policies.title: Nepal: ordinary passports eligible for tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Nepal's current tourist-visa guidance and TIA's exhaustive exception list support visa on arrival for all listed foreign ordinary passports except India and the twelve prior-visa nationalities.
conditions: For ordinary short-visit/tourist treatment, TIA facilitates visa on arrival; the listed twelve nationalities in the separate prior-visa policy are expressly ineligible for arrival issuance, and Indian citizens are visa-free.

DoI's online tourist form may be completed before arrival or at airport kiosks, then the traveller pays at the counter and the immigration officer issues the visa. This is arrival processing, not a nationality-wide eVisa classification.
Tourist visa-on-arrival options are 15, 30 or 90 days; tourist stay, including extensions, is subject to Nepal's stated visa-year limits and immigration determination.

SAARC nationals Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Pakistan and Sri Lanka receive a gratis visa for up to 30 days on their first visit in a visa year; this is a fee-free visa on arrival, not no-visa admission. Afghanistan remains a named arrival-visa exclusion.

China, child, NRN-card, diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, study, transit, crew, special-document and case-specific rules are not flattened into this ordinary-passport nationality result.

policies.title: Nepal: SAARC ordinary passports with fee-free tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Nepal grants these non-Indian, non-Afghan SAARC citizens a gratis visa for up to 30 days on the first visit of a visa year.
conditions: This is a fee-free tourist visa, not no-visa entry, and is limited to up to 30 days on the first visit in a given visa year.
Afghanistan is a SAARC member but is expressly ineligible for visa on arrival and is therefore excluded from this group; Indian citizens are separately visa-free.
All ordinary-passport arrival conditions and exclusions of the overlapping universal visa-on-arrival policy continue to apply.

policies.title: Nepal: ordinary passports not eligible for visa on arrival
policies.summary: TIA Immigration expressly excludes these nationalities from visa on arrival; obtain an appropriate visitor visa before travel.
conditions: TIA Immigration expressly names these nationalities as not eligible for visa on arrival. They require an appropriate visa arranged before travel through Nepal's pre-departure visa channels.

This policy does not call an online form eVisa: DoI's ordinary tourist online form is also used for counter-issued visa-on-arrival processing, and the reviewed sources do not establish an exclusive nationality-wide electronic issuance route for this group.
Does not decide diplomatic, official, service, special-document, refugee, residence, work, study, crew, transit or case-specific treatment.

policies.title: Maldives: foreign ordinary passports with tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Maldives Immigration grants the tourist visa on arrival to foreign tourists without visa pre-approval, subject to the separate Israeli-passport prohibition.
conditions: Applies only to foreign ordinary passports for tourism/short visitor travel. Maldives Immigration says tourist visas are granted on arrival and tourists do not require visa pre-approval.
A Traveller Declaration is mandatory within 96 hours before the arriving flight and is a free self-declaration. It is not an ETA or eVisa and does not replace arrival issuance.

Arrival requires an MRZ passport or travel document with at least one month validity (no extended-validity passports), a complete itinerary with confirmed return journey, prepaid registered accommodation and sufficient funds, or a pre-approved Maldives Immigration sponsorship visa; onward-entry requirements and applicable yellow-fever certification also apply.
Immigration officers determine admissibility at the port of entry. The reviewed current tourist-visa page does not state a fixed initial tourist-visa duration, so this candidate does not infer one.

Does not classify residence, work, business, meeting/conference, dependent, marriage, transit without clearing arrival immigration, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, emergency or other special-document cases.

policies.title: Maldives: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: The destination's own ordinary-passport code is represented as citizenship rather than a foreign-entry visa result.
conditions: This represents a Maldivian citizen holding an ordinary Maldivian passport, not foreign visitor admission.
Does not classify dual-nationality, foreign residence, diplomatic, official, emergency or other document-specific circumstances.

policies.title: Seychellois nationals: outside foreign visitor-entry scope
policies.summary: The visitor permit and foreign-visitor Travel Authorisation framework does not establish entry requirements for Seychellois nationals travelling on a Seychelles passport.
conditions: This classification does not establish the departure-form, carrier, document, dual-nationality, permit-holder, or admission treatment of a particular Seychellois national.
The Electronic Border System separately describes an Embarkation Information Form for Seychellois citizens and permit holders leaving Seychelles; it is not a visitor ETA classification.

policies.title: All foreign ordinary passports: no visa, mandatory pre-travel ETA and visitor permit on arrival
policies.summary: Seychelles does not require an entry visa regardless of nationality and issues the Visitor's Permit on arrival, but every foreign ordinary visitor must first obtain a Travel Authorisation/ETA before departure. The mandatory pre-travel authorization is normalized as eta.
conditions: Seychelles' Immigration guidance expressly distinguishes a no-visa system from the mandatory pre-departure Electronic Travel Authorisation. For this repository's access taxonomy, the live mandatory ETA is the operative entry status and supersedes an otherwise visa_free label; it does not turn the Visitor's Permit into a visa on arrival or an eVisa.

The Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival, initially for up to three months and free for that first period. It may be extended in successive periods of up to three months to a maximum of twelve months if the visitor continues to meet the conditions; each extension costs SCR 5,000.

A visitor must not be a prohibited immigrant or already hold a permit entitling residence; must have a valid return/onward ticket, confirmed accommodation and sufficient funds. Immigration's general entry guidance states a minimum of US$150 or equivalent per day.

The visitor route covers holiday, pleasure, business, and visits to friends/family. It does not permit paid or unpaid full-time or part-time work by a non-Seychellois; a Gainful Occupation Permit is separate. Residence, student, dependant, international-trade-zone, crew, maritime, diplomatic, transit, refugee, alien-document, laissez-passer, and other special-document cases are not established by this ordinary visitor policy.

A valid passport or other Seychelles-recognised travel document is required and must remain valid through the intended stay and return to the country of origin/residence. A yellow-fever certificate is required only for a traveller resident in, recently visiting, or transiting more than 12 hours through a listed endemic-risk country.

Use the Seychelles e-Border app or seychelles.govtas.com before departure. The current portal permits a Travel Authorisation application within 30 days of scheduled arrival and requires the passport page, traveller photo, trip information, health/customs answers and payment; permit holders additionally upload the applicable permit.

Official government pages publish inconsistent standard TA fee/application-window wording: Tourism Seychelles states €10, while MFA states EUR 10.90 and says up to 10 days before flight. Treat the live official portal checkout and current carrier instructions as controlling for price and timing; neither discrepancy changes the mandatory-ETA status.

application.label: Seychelles Electronic Border System Travel Authorisation
steps: Apply through the government-linked Seychelles e-Border app or seychelles.govtas.com before departure.
Upload the passport page and traveller photo, provide trip and required health/customs information, upload supporting trip/permit information, and pay the applicable charge.
Travel only with a valid authorization and present the return/onward ticket, accommodation and financial evidence needed for the Visitor's Permit on arrival.

policies.title: Trinidad and Tobago nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: The Immigration Division's eVisa service applies to eligible foreign nationals, not nationals presenting a Trinidad and Tobago passport.
conditions: This does not establish treatment for a dual national presenting another passport, residence, work, departure controls, or individual border admission.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

policies.title: Named non-CARICOM ordinary passports: visa exemption
policies.summary: The Immigration Division's current visa-exempt-country list expressly says these named nationalities do not require a visa for entry to Trinidad and Tobago.
conditions: The current official list establishes no common visitor-stay duration, work right, residence right, transit rule, or special-document treatment for this mixed nationality cohort.

This policy is confined to the named ordinary-passport nationalities. It does not extend the country list to other Commonwealth, territorial, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, crew, or travel-document holders.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

policies.title: Named CARICOM ordinary passports: visa exemption and six-month definite entry
policies.summary: The Immigration Division lists these CARICOM nationalities as visa-exempt; Foreign Ministry CSME guidance says a CARICOM national seeking entry receives a definite six-month entry subject to immigration requirements.
conditions: The stated six months is subject to satisfaction of all immigration requirements and does not itself establish entry, employment, residence, a work-permit exemption, or an indefinite CSME Skills Certificate stay.
Free movement for listed CSME skill categories requires the appropriate Skills Certificate; other CARICOM nationals seeking employment must apply for a work permit.
This policy covers only the common ordinary-passport visitor component, not diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, crew, or other special documents.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

policies.title: United Kingdom and European Union ordinary passports: visa exemption
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry's current visa instructions expressly say that United Kingdom passport holders and European Union member-country holders do not require visas to visit Trinidad and Tobago.
conditions: The instructions do not provide a shared visitor-stay duration or establish employment, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.
Ireland and the United Kingdom also appear on Immigration's current visa-exempt-country list; this policy includes each code once as the explicit UK/EU group.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

policies.title: Explicitly named ordinary passports: electronic visitor visa required
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry visa instructions directly identify these nationalities as requiring a visa, and state that all Trinidad and Tobago entry visas are electronic; they are normalized as eVisa.
conditions: China, Taiwan, Cuba, North Korea, and Vietnam are expressly named in the current instructions' visa-required applicant cohort; Venezuela is expressly stated to require a visa for entry. The regional references to Asian, African, Middle-East and Far-East countries are not used to infer any additional code.

The Immigration Division eVisa service is for eligible foreign nationals from visa-required countries. Applicants need a passport valid at least six months, email address, digital photograph, supporting PDFs, and a Visa or Mastercard; approval is sent by email.

The official portal currently lists a TTD 800 multiple-entry eVisa fee, while ttconnect describes a TTD 400 fee. This official fee discrepancy is unresolved and does not alter the eVisa classification.

Bona fide operating aircraft or seagoing-vessel crew do not require a visa regardless of nationality; that occupation-specific exception is not a nationality-wide ordinary visitor rule. Possession of an eVisa does not guarantee admission.
This does not establish work, residence, student, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, or other special-document treatment.

From 17 March 2026, all persons entering or leaving Trinidad and Tobago must complete the free online Arrival/Departure Card before travel (up to 72 hours) and present its QR-code receipt. This is a travel declaration, not a visa, ETA, or entry guarantee.

application.label: Trinidad and Tobago Immigration Division eVisa Online Services
steps: Confirm that the passport nationality is subject to a visa requirement and meets the online-service eligibility screening.
Prepare the required passport, digital photograph, supporting documents, email address, and payment card.
Apply through the Immigration Division eVisa portal, receive the approved eVisa by email, print it, and present it with the Arrival/Departure Card receipt to border officers.

policies.title: Samoa: free Visitor’s Permit on arrival for foreign ordinary passports
policies.summary: Samoa Immigration says foreign nationals without Samoan citizenship or temporary residence receive a free Visitor’s Permit when they arrive, subject to entry requirements.
conditions: Ordinary-passport short-visit classification only. Samoa Immigration states a destination-wide rule for foreign nationals who do not hold Samoan citizenship or a valid Temporary Resident Permit.

The Visitor’s Permit is issued upon arrival and is therefore normalized as visa on arrival, even though it is free and a Samoa Tourism Authority page describes short visits as not requiring an entry permit in advance.

Current Samoa Immigration guidance states 90 days. The Samoa Tourism Authority page still states less than 60 days; travellers should verify the permitted duration with Samoa Immigration because the official pages conflict.

Entry requires a return or onward ticket, a passport valid for at least six months after intended departure, permission for the onward destination, accommodation details and evidence of sufficient funds.
Grant remains subject to health, character, deportation-record, warning-list and immigration-clearance requirements and is not automatic admission.
Does not decide residence, employment, study, longer visits, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document, American Samoa territorial-national, emergency or case-specific treatment.

policies.title: Madagascar: short-stay visa on arrival for foreign ordinary passports
policies.summary: Madagascar requires every non-Malagasy nationality to hold a visa but permits the short-stay visa process at international airports and ports, with online pre-application as an optional alternative.
conditions: Ordinary-passport tourism and other eligible non-immigrant short visits only. The reviewed Embassy guidance says every non-Malagasy nationality needs a visa and describes the short-stay visa as available at Madagascar's international airports and ports.

The Ministry of Tourism says a single-entry stay visa may be requested at the arrival airport or online. Because no advance authorisation is necessary when using the arrival route, this policy is normalized as visa on arrival rather than eVisa.

Decree No. 2017-1021 applies the eVisa system to every foreign non-immigrant and permits instructions online or at arrival. An online landing authorisation is not a travel document or a guarantee that the border visa will be granted.

Current consular requirements include a completed form, recent photographs, an ordinary passport valid more than six months after the return date with at least two blank pages, return travel, accommodation, and payment of the applicable visa fee.
Short-stay visas may be extended only within a cumulative 90-day maximum, are not convertible to long-stay status, and do not authorize paid or profit-making activity.
Yellow-fever certification may be required after recent presence in an infected country. Border officers retain admissibility authority.

Does not classify immigration, residence, employment, study exceeding short-stay scope, transit without border clearance, crew, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless or other special-document cases.

application.label: Official eVisa Madagascar delegated-service portal
steps: Choose either the border application route or the optional online process linked by the Ministry of Tourism.
For online pre-application, submit the requested identity, passport, trip and accommodation information and retain the landing authorisation.
At the entry point, present the required original documents, landing authorisation if used, and payment receipt or complete the arrival application and fee payment with immigration officers.

policies.title: Madagascar: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A Malagasy citizen using an ordinary Madagascar national passport is represented as citizenship rather than foreign visitor admission.
conditions: Represents an ordinary Madagascar national passport holder returning to Madagascar, not the diplomatic, service or foreign visitor categories.
Does not classify dual-nationality, foreign residence, document-validity or case-specific border circumstances.

policies.title: Palauan nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: The Immigration Division directs Palauan citizens to use a Palauan passport to enter and leave Palau; foreign-national visitor visa rules do not determine their entry.
conditions: Palau permits dual citizenship, but this classification does not determine a dual national's entry when presenting another passport or any departure, residence, security, or individual-admissibility decision.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Federated States of Micronesia, Marshall Islands, and United States ordinary passports: visa exemption
policies.summary: Palau expressly exempts citizens of the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the United States from a visa to visit, work, or reside, subject to Palauan law.
conditions: The authority states that this exemption is effective from 2 November 2022 and allows visit, work, or residence only in accordance with Palauan law. It is not a passport-wide grant of work authorisation independent of those laws.
The traveller needs a passport valid at least six months, must state the purpose of visit, and is not required to hold an onward ticket under this specific route.
This does not establish treatment of U.S. military personnel, diplomatic missions, dependants, special travel documents, or non-citizen residents; those are separate status-specific rules.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Schengen-contracting-state ordinary passports: 90-day visa waiver
policies.summary: Citizens of the named Schengen Agreement contracting states may enter Palau without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
conditions: This is the mutual Palau-European Union waiver as described by the Immigration Division. It applies to citizens of the named Schengen-contracting states; Cyprus is not added without an express current source classification.
The page does not make this tourist waiver an employment, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, or other special-document entitlement.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passports: 30-day visa waiver
policies.summary: Palau's Immigration Division states that the Palau-Russia mutual waiver permits Russian citizens to stay without a visa for 30 days.
conditions: This classification is limited to the stated 30-day visa waiver and does not establish work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, or special-document treatment.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Taiwan ordinary passports: conditional visa waiver
policies.summary: Taiwan nationals may use Palau's bilateral visa-free arrangement when they meet the stated passport, purpose, return-ticket, and onward-destination requirements.
conditions: The waiver accepts ordinary, official, or diplomatic passports with at least six months' validity; this policy models only an ordinary passport.
The traveller must not intend to work, study, or reside in Palau, and must hold a return-flight ticket and a valid visa for the onward destination.
No stay duration is stated in this bilateral-waiver passage. Other visitor, security, admission, and special-document requirements remain separate.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Bangladesh and Myanmar ordinary passports: visitor visa before travel
policies.summary: Palau Immigration expressly says Bangladesh and Myanmar nationals must apply for a visa before reaching Palau, rather than use the ordinary visitor visa-on-arrival process.
conditions: Applicants should contact a Palau diplomatic mission, representative authority, or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs from their country of residence. The authority does not establish an eVisa or visa-on-arrival option for these ordinary passports.

Both nationalities also appear in the current flagged-country pre-clearance process. Complete applications must be submitted at least five days before travel, and incomplete submissions may lead to denied boarding or refusal of entry.

Any approval remains subject to document validity, stated purpose, accommodation, funds, onward travel, security, and the Director's assessment. Work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, or special-document routes are separate.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Flagged ordinary passports: mandatory pre-clearance before visitor visa on arrival
policies.summary: The named nationalities must obtain written Palau pre-clearance before travel; their ordinary short-visitor visa is otherwise the Immigration Division's visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: This ETA normalization represents the notice's mandatory advance pre-clearance, not an electronic visa: carriers must not board a flagged traveller without written confirmation of clearance. The visitor visa itself remains issued on arrival under the general rule.

Submit the completed pre-clearance application, Palau Entry Form submission, passport bio-page, non-refundable return ticket, accommodation proof, and sufficient-funds proof to immtravelapproval@bcbp.pw at least five days before travel.
Under the notice, entry is only for the duration on the return ticket and no more than 30 days; no extension is granted unless approved through a formal visa or permit process.
This does not classify separate invitation-based, diplomatic, medical-emergency, government-invited-delegation, work, residence, transit, crew, official, or special-document cases.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Cyprus ordinary passports: reciprocal EU–Palau visa waiver
policies.summary: The reciprocal EU–Palau agreement covers citizens of Cyprus even though Palau's live Schengen-contracting-state list omits Cyprus.
conditions: The agreement covers valid ordinary passports and short stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
Paid activity is excluded, and ordinary border-entry conditions and refusal powers remain applicable.
The treaty is controlling legal evidence for Cyprus; the Immigration page's separately worded Schengen list does not repeal or narrow it.

policies.title: Other ordinary foreign passports: 30-day tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Palau's Immigration Division says a tourist visa may be issued on arrival to short-term genuine visitors; this explicitly bounded complement excludes every stated visa-waiver, pre-clearance, and advance-visa cohort.
conditions: The visitor must genuinely intend tourism, leisure, or a social visit and must not perform work. The initial tourist visa is 30 days and may be extended twice for 30 days each by applying at least seven days before expiry.

The traveller needs a passport valid at least six months, an onward or return ticket unless exempt, sufficient funds, and any other travel evidence or circumstances acceptable to the Director. Visa issuance and border admission remain discretionary.

Business, work, student, missionary, foreign-government/international-organization, resident, investor, dependent, diplomatic, crew, transit, emergency, refugee, stateless, official, service, and other special-document arrangements are separate and not established by this ordinary tourist classification.
Diplomats recognized by the Ministry of State and their families, and holders of a Presidential or Director exemption letter, have separate visa and onward-ticket exceptions.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Vanuatu: listed exempt ordinary passports with tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Although the country list calls these nationalities exempt from a visitor visa, DIPS expressly issues the tourist visa to them upon arrival.
conditions: This is an arrival-issued tourist visa, not true no-visa admission: DIPS says exempt-country travellers can obtain the tourist visa upon arrival.
Tourism, leisure and social visits only; the stated stay is up to 120 days, with no extension or status change, and no commercial, employment or business activity.
The traveller must meet DIPS grant criteria including character, health, security, funds, genuine departure intent, onward/return transport and parental/guardian consent where applicable.
Non-citizens need a valid passport or travel document with more than six months validity, a return airline ticket, and confirmed accommodation or a local address.
Does not decide visitor visa (30-day), transit (airside up to 24 hours), residence, work, study, close-family, descent, diplomatic, official, special-document, or case-specific rules.

policies.title: Vanuatu: listed non-exempt ordinary passports requiring tourist visa approval before travel
policies.summary: DIPS states that non-exempt-country nationals must apply in advance and obtain approval before travelling.
conditions: DIPS says these non-exempt nationalities must apply for and obtain tourist-visa approval before travel; the application is subject to the stated tourist grant criteria.

The eVisa-branded online application portal is an application route. The reviewed DIPS pages do not establish a nationality-wide electronic visa issued in lieu of the required pre-approval, so this is not classified as eVisa.
Tourist visas allow up to 120 days without extension or status change and prohibit commercial, employment and business activity.
Transit, visitor (30-day), residence, work, study, diplomatic, official, special-document, and individual admissibility rules remain separate.

application.label: Vanuatu Immigration online visa application portal
steps: Select the tourist visa application route for a non-exempt nationality.
Submit the completed application and supporting passport, travel, funds, health, character and departure-intent documents.
Obtain approval before travelling to Vanuatu.

policies.title: Vanuatu: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: The destination's own code is represented as citizenship, not a foreign-entry visa result.
conditions: Represents a Ni-Vanuatu citizen using a Vanuatu passport or qualifying identity/travel document.
Does not decide dual nationality, foreign residence, diplomatic, official, emergency or other special-document cases.

policies.title: Cabo Verde nationals: outside foreign visitor-entry scope
policies.summary: The published foreign-citizen visa framework does not establish visitor admission requirements for holders of a Cabo Verde passport.
conditions: Cabo Verde nationals are exempt from EASE pre-registration; their international-passport holders are also exempt from TSA.

A natural-born Cabo Verdean travelling on a foreign passport, and qualifying spouse or descendant, has a distinct evidence-based exemption; this citizenship evidence is not a nationality-wide foreign-passport rule.

policies.title: Listed foreign nationalities: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Portal Único's current visa-exemption schedule expressly lists these nationalities and their maximum exemption periods. EASE pre-registration and the Airport Security Tax remain separate travel/security formalities, not an ETA or visa decision.
conditions: The maximum exemption is 30 days for AD, AT, BE, BR, BG, CA, CN, HR, CY, CZ, DK, EE, FI, FR, DE, GR, HK, HU, IS, IE, IT, LV, LI, LT, LU, MT, MC, MA, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SM, SG, SK, SI, ZA, ES, SE, CH, TL, GB, US and VA; 60 days for RU and ST; 90 days for BJ, BF, GM, GH, GN, CI, LR, MO, ML, NE, NG, KR and TG; and 180 days for AO, GW, MZ and UA.

Before travel, the schedule directs listed citizens to pre-register through EASE and, where applicable, pay TSA up to five days before arrival. The consular FAQ describes pre-registration as supplying flight, exit and accommodation data for prior security verification; it is not described as an authorization or visa grant, so this policy remains visa_free rather than eta.

The consular portal says foreign travellers generally must pre-register and pay TSA, but exempts Cabo Verde nationals/natural-born persons and foreign legal residents from pre-registration. TSA exemptions include children under two, qualifying official missions, forced technical/weather landings and airport transit.

The exemption schedule says a stay beyond the stated period requires a visa from the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post. The general visitor framework requires a passport valid at least three months at the time of stay.

This ordinary-passport nationality policy does not determine admission for residents, laissez-passer holders, foreign-mission or international-organization staff, refugee travel-document holders, natural-born Cabo Verdeans travelling on another passport, diplomatic/official/courtesy travel, residence, work, crew or transit cases.

policies.title: Listed foreign nationalities: advance visa required
policies.summary: Portal Único's current compulsory-visa schedule says these citizens must obtain a visa at the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post before travelling. The official materials do not establish a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival or eVisa route for this cohort.
conditions: Obtain the entry visa before travel at the nearest Cabo Verde embassy or consular post, then pre-register on EASE and, where applicable, pay TSA up to five days before arrival.

The consular FAQ says visa applications use an internet platform and may exceptionally be made at embassies, consular posts or in Cabo Verde with a surcharge. That generic processing statement does not prove that every listed nationality receives an eVisa, so the classification is not evisa.

The consular portal's frontier-visa statement is limited to citizens resident in countries where Cabo Verde has no diplomatic representation; it is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival rule for this policy cohort.

Tourism visas cover recreation and cruises, are to be used within 60 days of grant, permit 90 days and may be extended up to an equal period. Transit visas are distinct, last four days and may be extended once. Official, diplomatic, courtesy, temporary and residence visas have separate purpose and duration rules.

This policy does not override valid-residence, free-movement/agreement, laissez-passer, foreign-mission/organization staff, refugee-travel-document, natural-born Cabo Verdean family, diplomatic/official, transit, work, study or residence exceptions.

policies.title: Mozambique: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A Mozambique citizen using a normal national passport is represented as citizenship rather than foreign visitor admission.
conditions: Represents a Mozambique national returning on a normal national passport, not a foreign visitor or special-document route.
Does not classify dual-nationality, foreign residence, document-validity or case-specific border circumstances.

policies.title: Mozambique: longstanding all-passport visa-exemption partners
policies.summary: Both the live immigration portal and the Foreign Ministry identify these nationalities as exempt from a visa for qualifying short visits.
conditions: The live portal permits the stated ordinary-passport tourist or business stay without an eTA or eVisa: 90 days for Botswana and Tanzania, and 30 days for the other listed nationalities.
The Foreign Ministry describes these as all-passport bilateral visa-suppression agreements.

Ordinary-passport short tourism or business visits only; work, residence, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency and other special-document cases are outside this policy.
Admission remains subject to passport validity, travel-purpose, supporting-document, health, security and border-control requirements; an approval or exemption does not guarantee entry.

policies.title: Mozambique: additional current ordinary-passport visa exemptions
policies.summary: The live immigration portal lists these ordinary or all-passport nationalities as visa-exempt for qualifying short tourist or business visits.
conditions: The live portal lists 30 days for Angola, Cabo Verde, Lesotho, Namibia, São Tomé and Príncipe, Seychelles and Uganda, and 90 days for Kenya and Rwanda.

The Foreign Ministry's separate current entry-visas page still publishes only eight longstanding all-passport agreements and omits this expanded cohort. The live National Immigration Service eligibility table is treated as the current operational rule, but this official-source discrepancy warrants rechecking.

Ordinary-passport short tourism or business visits only; work, residence, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency and other special-document cases are outside this policy.
Admission remains subject to passport validity, travel-purpose, supporting-document, health, security and border-control requirements; an approval or exemption does not guarantee entry.

policies.title: Mozambique: eTA required before travel
policies.summary: The live immigration portal requires these nationalities to obtain an electronic travel authorisation before qualifying short tourist or business travel.
conditions: The eTA permits up to 30 days for tourist or business purposes and applies to all passport types in the published table; this policy models the ordinary-passport component.
The applicant must apply online, pay the fee and carry the approved preliminary eTA PDF for boarding and arrival.
An eVisa is needed instead if the permitted ETA duration or purpose does not cover the trip.

Ordinary-passport short tourism or business visits only; work, residence, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency and other special-document cases are outside this policy.
Admission remains subject to passport validity, travel-purpose, supporting-document, health, security and border-control requirements; an approval or exemption does not guarantee entry.

application.label: Start from Mozambique's official National Immigration Service eVisa and eTA portal
steps: Confirm the passport nationality, intended purpose and permitted stay in the official eligibility table.
Complete the linked online application, upload the requested documents and pay the applicable fee.
If approved, download and print the preliminary eVisa or eTA PDF and carry it for boarding and arrival.

policies.title: Mozambique: advance electronic visa route
policies.summary: The live immigration portal includes these ordinary-passport nationalities in Mozambique's electronic-visa scheme for qualifying visits.
conditions: The tourist eVisa covers tourism, holidays or vacations of 90 days or less; other published electronic-visa purposes have their own requirements.
The applicant must apply and pay online before travel, then carry the approved preliminary eVisa PDF for boarding and arrival.
The physical visa may be finalized at the border, but prior electronic approval is mandatory, so this is normalized as eVisa rather than visa on arrival.

Ordinary-passport short tourism or business visits only; work, residence, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency and other special-document cases are outside this policy.
Admission remains subject to passport validity, travel-purpose, supporting-document, health, security and border-control requirements; an approval or exemption does not guarantee entry.

application.label: Start from Mozambique's official National Immigration Service eVisa and eTA portal
steps: Confirm the passport nationality, intended purpose and permitted stay in the official eligibility table.
Complete the linked online application, upload the requested documents and pay the applicable fee.
If approved, download and print the preliminary eVisa or eTA PDF and carry it for boarding and arrival.

policies.title: Mozambique: embassy visa required before travel
policies.summary: The live immigration portal says these nationalities cannot use its eVisa service and must request a visa from the nearest embassy.
conditions: The traveller must obtain the appropriate visa through a Mozambique embassy before travel; nationality alone does not establish an electronic or arrival route.

Ordinary-passport short tourism or business visits only; work, residence, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency and other special-document cases are outside this policy.
Admission remains subject to passport validity, travel-purpose, supporting-document, health, security and border-control requirements; an approval or exemption does not guarantee entry.

policies.title: Ugandan nationals: outside foreign visitor-entry scope
policies.summary: The foreign-national visa and eVisa framework does not establish a visitor-entry classification for an Ugandan passport holder.
conditions: This classification does not determine a dual citizen's treatment when travelling on a foreign passport, nor border admissibility in a particular case.

policies.title: Named foreign nationalities: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Uganda's live NCIC schedule expressly says nationals of these 40 listed countries or regions do not require a visa. The classification is visa_free, not a visa on arrival.
conditions: The current NCIC schedule frames the exemption as visa-abolition agreements. It does not publish a common ordinary-visitor duration, purpose or work entitlement; confirm the admission stamp and agreement-specific conditions at entry.

The archived 2021 visa-prone notice has a different 39-country list: it includes AO, CU and LY, but not the live schedule's CD, MZ, AE or HK. The live NCIC schedule controls current nationality scope; the 2021 notice supports online-processing mechanics only.

For EAC travel, the Kigali High Commission says Rwanda and Kenya citizens may enter with a valid national identity card or e-passport; Burundi and Tanzania citizens are exempt with a valid e-passport or laissez-passer. This ordinary-passport policy does not convert those alternative documents into a residence right.

A visa-exempt national holding a valid Conventional Travel Document is also exempt from the online visa requirement. Treatment of other refugee, alien, emergency or special documents is not established here.

The NCIC page separately exempts diplomatic/official passports of DZ, CU, EG, ET, IN, IR, RU, SN, ZA, TR (diplomatic only), VE and VN, plus named international-organization laissez-passers on official business. Those exceptions do not broaden ordinary-passport access.

Valid Kenya, Rwanda or Uganda resident-permit holders travelling within those territories can obtain an InterState Pass at entry; that residence exception does not apply to travel into Uganda from outside Kenya or Rwanda.
Visa-free status does not authorize employment, study, residence, work, crew, transit, diplomatic/official travel, East African Tourist Visa travel, or otherwise inadmissible entry.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: The live complete no-visa schedule identifies the ordinary foreign passports that do not need a visa. For the remaining ordinary foreign passports, NCIC's online process requires a Travel Authorization/Visa Approval Letter before travel and does not issue normal visas on arrival; the complement is normalized as evisa.
conditions: Apply through visas.immigration.go.ug and obtain the Travel Authorization/Visa Approval Letter before boarding. The 2021 NCIC notice says there are no normal visas issued on arrival; the current Abuja High Commission page says all visa applications use the same electronic system. This is evisa rather than eta or visa_on_arrival.

The changed 2021 nationality list is not used to construct this complement: current scope comes from the live 40-country NCIC schedule, while the 2021 notice only corroborates the online approval and no-visa-on-arrival process.

The ordinary/tourist single-entry route covers tourism, medical treatment and family visits; it may be granted up to three months. The published fee is USD 50, approval is valid 90 days, and the initial period may be extended by another 60 days in two intervals.

Use a passport valid at least six months and upload the passport biodata page, itinerary/tour plan, recent photo and accommodation evidence; purpose-specific invitations/status documents and yellow-fever evidence may be required.
Carry the approval letter, passport, payment evidence and uploaded documents to border control for biometric capture. Approval does not guarantee admission; immigration decides at entry.
Transit is a separate online visa capped at seven days and non-extendable. The East African Tourist Visa and employment, residence, student, dependant and special passes are distinct routes.

This complement excludes named nationality exemptions, qualifying CTDs, EAC identity-card/e-passport or laissez-passer travel, EAC-resident InterState Passes, diplomatic/official passports, international-organization laissez-passers, British military personnel and specifically authorized temporary operational exceptions.

application.label: Uganda Electronic Visa/Permit Application System
application.processingTime: NCIC's online-visa notice says decisions take 2–3 days and advises applying at least ten days before travel; Kigali High Commission says typically 2–3 working days and recommends five working days.
steps: Start a Visa application on the official system and select the ordinary/tourist category and purpose.
Complete the form, upload the passport, photo and purpose-specific documents, and make required payment.
Receive the Travel Authorization/Visa Approval Letter and carry it with the submitted evidence to border control.

policies.title: Benin: current named ordinary-passport visa waivers
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry agreement register expressly identifies these ordinary- or national-passport waiver entries, including the current UEMOA/ECOWAS free-movement entries.
conditions: The current Foreign Ministry register, not the 2020 general flyer, is the operative support for this named ordinary-passport cohort. It records both the country and the passport types covered by each agreement.
The reciprocal entries cover HT, HK, SG, BZ, DM, GD, MH, FM, AG, BS, BB, MY, PH and VC; its stated periods are 14 days for HK, 14 days for SG, 30 days for MY and PH, and three months for the others.

The UEMOA/ECOWAS entries cover SL, BF, CI, GW, ML, NE, SN, TG, CV, GM, NG, LR, GH and GN. The register identifies the applicable ECOWAS Protocol or UEMOA Treaty; duration and any travel-document conditions must be confirmed with the competent authorities.

The African-agreement entries cover ZA, TN, RW, CF, TD, CG, MU, ST, SC, KE and BI. Their register entries expressly include a national or ordinary passport and generally state three months, except ZA states one month.

The September 2020 MAEC flyer claiming a unilateral 53-African-country waiver is retained as historical official evidence but is not promoted for its other 28 codes. The current register lists several of those countries only for diplomatic/service passports and does not reproduce a 53-country unilateral rule.

This policy does not establish employment, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic/official, special-document, health, document-validity, prior-history, public-order, national-security or case-specific admissibility treatment. The separate 72-hour cruise exemption requires an approved travel agency.

policies.title: Benin: Beninese ordinary passport
policies.summary: A Beninese ordinary passport is issued to persons of Beninese nationality; this is not foreign visitor admission.
conditions: Applies to Beninese citizens holding an ordinary Beninese passport.
Does not decide dual-nationality document choice, foreign residence, or foreign-passport entry conditions.

policies.title: Antigua and Barbuda nationals: outside foreign visitor scope
policies.summary: The foreign-national visa routes do not establish a visitor-entry classification for an Antigua and Barbuda passport holder.
conditions: This does not determine the treatment of a dual national travelling on a foreign passport or any individual departure, document, security or admission requirement.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free visitors
policies.summary: The current Immigration Department list expressly names these ordinary-passport nationalities as not requiring a visa. China and Cuba have a distinct 30-day cap; other listed visitors are normally admitted for holiday or business for up to six months if the published conditions are met.
conditions: China and Cuba are exempt only where travel does not exceed 30 days. The live list's section heading calls its other named European group EU but also names Serbia; this policy follows the explicit country names, not the inaccurate regional label.

For other named nationals, holiday or business stays may not exceed six months and require a valid passport, onward/return ticket, accommodation confirmation and evidence of funds. Admission remains discretionary.
This does not establish work, residence, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance eVisa
policies.summary: The Immigration Department explicitly says countries not in its visa-exempt lists require a visa, and its eVisa Unit processes online applications for every person who requires one. The nationality complement is therefore normalized as evisa.
conditions: Apply electronically through the Immigration Department's entry-eVisa route. The eVisa is an official entry document, obtained after the Department decides the online application and paid electronically; it is not an ETA.

The eVisa FAQ says the route is for a travel-document holder requiring a visa and that a traveller who arrives without a visa is undocumented and may be refused entry. The baseline status is therefore not visa_on_arrival.

A separate, conditional 30-day tourist visa on arrival may be granted to a visitor who holds a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa or permanent-resident card, has no Antigua and Barbuda residence/occupation, travels solely for tourism/casual visits, and has a passport valid at least six months. This document-based exception does not change the nationality baseline.

The eVisa application requires a passport/travel document valid at least six months, photo, journey evidence, accommodation or sponsor evidence, funds and other requested documents. It is for tourism; work, residence, student, transit, cruise, diplomatic, official, special-document and admission cases remain separate.

A normally visa-required cruise visitor arriving in the morning and departing that evening, or a same-day in-transit passenger remaining in the airport's controlled space with onward proof, has a narrow special exception not represented by this ordinary visitor policy.

application.label: Antigua and Barbuda entry eVisa application
application.processingTime: The Immigration Department FAQ states a decision within seven working days, potentially extended to 15 days or, exceptionally, 30 days.
steps: Apply through the Immigration Department entry-eVisa route before travel.
Upload the required passport, photo, trip, accommodation/sponsor and financial evidence, then pay electronically.
Carry the approved eVisa and supporting travel documents to border control; the Department may still refuse admission.

policies.title: Colombia: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A Colombian citizen returns under Colombian citizenship and national-document rules rather than the foreign visitor-visa framework.
conditions: Colombian citizens have the right to enter and must identify themselves as Colombian when they also hold another nationality.
Check-Mig is optional and recommended; it is not an ETA or entry authorization.
Does not determine dual-national documentation, passport validity, minors' exit consent or case-specific border circumstances.

policies.title: Bahrain: citizenship treatment

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: arrival-issued visitor waiver or visa
policies.summary: The current Qatar Tourism passport wizard places these nationalities in arrival-entry paths. conditions: Passport-level routes vary: some are free arrival waivers, while IR, MU, ME, TW, PK, TH and UA are displayed with paid and/or Discover Qatar hotel-reservation arrival routes. Hayya A1/A2/A3 may be an advance alternative where the wizard says so; optional online processing does not replace an available arrival status.

Current MOI guidance requires a passport valid at least three months, onward/return ticket and compulsory health insurance for on-arrival visitors; particular routes also require a hotel booking, Discover Qatar booking, cash/card or fees. Check the live selector for the exact passport route and duration.

The older MOI 90-day schedule publishes six-month passport validity, onward ticket and a passport sticker; its duration lists do not exactly match the current Qatar Tourism selector. Treat the individual live selector and border decision as controlling.

A residence in GCC, or residence/valid visa in Schengen, UK, US, Australia, New Zealand or Canada, can create distinct document-conditioned A2/A3 routes. It is not a nationality-wide rule. Transit, Qatar-Oman joint visas, employment, residence, diplomatic/official, temporary travel documents and special cases are separate.

policies.title: Other passport codes listed by the visa wizard: advance Hayya eVisa

conditions: Apply for the A1 Entry Visa through Hayya before travel; the selector states that a hotel reservation is required during application and visa fee is payable after approval.

The eVisa route is for tourism and remains subject to passport, accommodation, insurance, funds, health, security and admission requirements. It does not create work, residence, transit, diplomatic/official or special-document rights.

application.label: Hayya Tourist E-Visas
steps: Select the appropriate A1 visitor route in Hayya before travel.
Provide the required hotel reservation and other requested travel documentation, then complete payment after approval as instructed.
Carry the approved electronic visa and supporting documents; admission remains subject to Qatar border control.

policies.title: Saudi nationals: outside foreign visitor scope

conditions: This does not determine a dual national’s treatment when presenting another passport, nor any case-specific exit, security or border requirement.
